claims.text: HEA coatings on transition-metal matrices exhibit a non-monotonic relationship between ambient temperature and tribological performance.
The initial improvement in tribological performance with temperature is caused by formation of a protective tribo-oxide layer.
Tribological performance degrades sharply above a critical temperature because the oxide becomes non-protective or the coating thermally softens.
The relevant initial state is a dense, single-phase or multiphase HEA coating with sub-micron-to-micron grains on a transition-metal substrate.
Increasing temperature transforms a hard protective oxide scale, such as Cr2O3 or Al2O3, into a soft, viscous, or delaminating oxide layer.
Elevated temperature causes thermal softening in the HEA coating subsurface.
Between 25°C and 500°C, frictional heating causes rapid formation of a dense, adherent oxide layer in AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5.
The protective oxide formed on AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 at elevated temperature increases wear resistance under atmospheric reciprocating sliding.
The protective oxide reduces the coefficient of friction as temperature increases.
Above the critical threshold, thermally activated plasticity and oxide instability cause oxide spalling or viscous behavior.
A temperature-induced decrease in coating yield strength leads to severe adhesive wear and material transfer.
Some refractory HEAs retain yield strengths above 500 MPa at 1200°C.
Wear resistance in the proposed coating system is limited more by tribo-oxide stability than by bulk yield strength.
The specific wear rate will decrease by a factor of 2–5 between 25°C and approximately 400°C.
Above approximately 400°C, the wear rate will increase exponentially.
Temperatures above the degradation boundary will produce catastrophic failure by severe adhesive wear.
The performance-degradation boundary is 550°C ± 50°C.
The proposed boundary corresponds to rapid diffusion-controlled oxidation producing porous, non-protective oxides and to a yield-strength drop below the stress needed to sustain the tribolayer.
Al additions stabilize protective oxides to higher temperatures than in Al-free HEAs.
Elevated-temperature phase decomposition, including a possible BCC-to-FCC transformation, can either improve or degrade wear resistance depending on alloy composition.

contradictions.description: The mechanism assigns the protective lower-temperature regime through 500°C, while the predicted outcome says wear begins increasing above approximately 400°C. The separately stated degradation boundary is 550°C ± 50°C, leaving an inconsistent onset between roughly 400°C and 500–600°C.
